ambiguous: task guardrails (Task guardrail=/guardrails=) are named 'guardrails' by the vendor but are output-side validation of TaskOutput after execution — an Effect-adjacent quality gate, NOT a rules/Decision surface and NOT action-side control

Task human_input is an Approval-shaped pause that occurs AFTER the task's tool effects — it belongs to the Approval layer by mechanism but witnesses a post-effect output review, never approval of a tool action
tool assignment (Agent tools=[...], Task tools=[...] override) is model-visibility scoping, not a Decision-layer decision: no per-call verdict, no argument inspection, no ask state
CodeInterpreterTool 'sandbox' fallback is a restricted in-process Python environment, not OS confinement; only its Docker strategy is container isolation, and unsafe_mode is neither
layer_vocabulary.notes: rules (the Decision layer): NOT covered — CrewAI has no declarative policy surface: no policy file, no allow/ask/deny rule language, no offline checker; the only pre-execution control is author-written PRE_TOOL_CALL hook code (arbitrary Python, fail-open on non-HookAborted exceptions), which is a property of a given program, not of the framework. approval (the Approval layer): Task human_input (post-task output review), Flow @human_feedback (step-boundary pause with recorded history), hook request_human_input inside PRE_TOOL_CALL (the only documented pre-action ask; exists only where an author wires it). sandbox (part of the Effect layer): no framework sandbox for ordinary in-process tools; CodeInterpreterTool offers Docker (recommended) / restricted-Python fallback / unsafe_mode strategies, selected at runtime and logged. effect (the Effect layer): tools execute in the user's own Python process with its filesystem/network/credential authority; outcomes observable via CrewOutput, the framework event bus, and external sentinel/sandbox-diff instrumentation.

measurement_route_evidence: No vendor decision checker and no declarative policy surface exist (DOC across the official docs/repo surface, 2026-10-22); the only pre-execution control is arbitrary author-written PRE_TOOL_CALL hook code, unevaluatable offline — the measurement design is therefore a live instrumented reference agent (source audit as A2-configured analog; witnessed asks as A3; sentinel/sandbox-diff as E1/E2), with no measurement run yet. (INFERENCE on DOC)

spike_answers.a_native_oracle: NO. CrewAI ships no check/evaluate/dry-run entrypoint, and more fundamentally no declarative policy artifact exists for one to evaluate: no policy file, no allow/ask/deny rule language appears anywhere in the official docs/repo surface consulted (DOC, 2026-10-22). The only pre-execution control is author-written hook code whose decision materializes only inside a live run.
spike_answers.b_documented_semantics: NO for Decision. A reconstructed route needs documented rule-matching semantics (patterns, precedence, no-match default); CrewAI documents none, because there are no rules. The precisely documented semantics are runtime mechanics — hook chain order and fail-open behaviour, human_input timing, guardrail signature/retry bound, @human_feedback pause/resume, tool execution locality — which suffice to DESIGN a live instrumented-reference-agent measurement, not to evaluate decisions offline. Modelling hook code offline and presenting it as the framework's decision is exactly the masquerade this program forbids.
spike_answers.c_surface_record: Surface: a Python library (Agent/Task/Crew/Flow) imported into the user's own program; canonical target is the OSS framework at 1.15.28, not the hosted AMP/Enterprise platform. Defaults: with no hooks registered, no tool call is gated — the model chooses from the agent's assigned tools (Agent tools=[...], narrowed by Task tools=[...]) and the framework executes in-process with the host process's authority; CodeInterpreterTool is the exception surface (Docker / restricted-Python / unsafe strategies). No verdicts issued; Decision route recorded as no paper surface.
